en: The Apadāna of the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya Kiṅkaṇipupphavagga 3 I offered a koraṇḍa flower to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher of the World. Because of that root of merit, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. Having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of suffering. This is my final existence. I have attained the state of peace. I am now a sage who has crossed over the flood. I have reached the further shore of the ocean of suffering. I am now one who has attained the goal. “In the past I was a forest-dweller,
living in dependence on my father and mother;
I lived by the slaughter of animals.”
"No wholesome merit exists for me.
Near my dwelling, the Leader of the World, the Three [Jewels], [resided].
Out of compassion, the One with Vision showed him three footprints;
and having seen the footprint that had been stepped upon, [he followed].
To the Teacher named Tissa,
with a joyful heart,
I gladdened my mind at his words.
Having seen a *koraṇḍa* tree in bloom growing from the earth,
he took it along with its own soil.
I worshipped the Best of Men.
By that well-performed deed,
and by my intention and aspiration;
Having abandoned the human body,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three.
Whichever womb I was reborn into, I—
Whether in the realm of the gods or among humans,
may I have skin the color of the koraṇḍaka flower and be exceedingly radiant.
In the ninety-two aeons since then,
because of the deed I performed back then,
I have not known a miserable rebirth.
This is the fruit of worshipping his feet:
the defilements have been burnt away by me... [and so forth].
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [as before] ...
This is the teaching of the Buddha.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Koraṇḍapupphiya recited these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Koraṇḍapupphiya.
